# Reclazz

**Free, open-source hot reload for Java, Spring and SAP Commerce.**
Edit, compile and see supported changes in the running JVM.

[Documentation](https://reclazz.com/docs/) · [Reload support](https://reclazz.com/docs/support-matrix/) · [Website](https://reclazz.com) · [Releases](https://github.com/onurkat/reclazz/releases)

## Documentation scope

Source version 1.4.1; evidence baseline 75535bd739d7eefd43523dcc63799436c472fe12; reviewed 2026-10-19.
Source presence does not establish release availability or acceptance on every runtime.
Read each support condition and verify the running application.

## Guides and references

- [Overview](https://reclazz.com/docs/): Make a change. Compile it. Keep the JVM running. Learn what Reclazz reloads, where the limits are, and how to verify the result.
- [Quickstart](https://reclazz.com/docs/quickstart/): Start with the route that launches your application JVM, then prove a changed response without restarting.
- [Reload support matrix](https://reclazz.com/docs/support-matrix/): Find the outcome, exact conditions and next action for the edit you want to make.
- [Java & JVM limits](https://reclazz.com/docs/java/): Understand method bodies, structural reload, field initialization, enum edits and reflective visibility.
- [Spring & MVC](https://reclazz.com/docs/spring/): Follow bean recreation, newly added components, MVC callbacks, advice, Jackson and constructor dependency boundaries.
- [Kafka, JMS & RabbitMQ](https://reclazz.com/docs/messaging/): Understand listener additions, consumer retirement, routing changes and the difference between direct saves and dependency cascades.
- [Configuration & resources](https://reclazz.com/docs/configuration/): Know which physical files are watched, how validation works, and when a configuration edit needs a restart.
- [SAP Commerce](https://reclazz.com/docs/sap-commerce/): Separate Java reload, platform generation, type-system updates and runtime configuration in the SAP development loop.
- [Persistence & caches](https://reclazz.com/docs/persistence/): Keep class replacement, ORM mapping, database schema and cached results separate when verifying a reload.
- [Reload timing](https://reclazz.com/docs/boundaries/): Choose immediate or request-boundary application, and understand pause, build holds and partial failures.
- [Agent options](https://reclazz.com/docs/configuration-reference/): Find every source-supported startup option, its default and the consequence of enabling it.
- [Troubleshooting](https://reclazz.com/docs/troubleshooting/): Diagnose the right process, watched output, pending restart and framework follow-up without guessing.
- [Versions & evidence](https://reclazz.com/docs/evidence/): Read support claims with their exact boundaries, inspect source and help keep the documentation honest.
- [Reference library](https://reclazz.com/docs/reference/): Complete configuration, behavior and scope reference: Documentation library.
- [Reproducible agentic workflow evaluation](https://reclazz.com/docs/reference/agentic-evaluation/): Complete configuration, behavior and scope reference: Reproducible agentic workflow evaluation.

- [Core JVM feature evidence](https://reclazz.com/docs/reference/feature-evidence/): Complete configuration, behavior and scope reference: Core JVM feature evidence.
- [For AI agents](https://reclazz.com/docs/reference/for-ai-agents/): Complete configuration, behavior and scope reference: For AI agents.
- [Reclazz Gradle plugin](https://reclazz.com/docs/reference/gradle-plugin/): Complete configuration, behavior and scope reference: Reclazz Gradle plugin.

- [Reclazz with Maven](https://reclazz.com/docs/reference/maven/): Complete configuration, behavior and scope reference: Reclazz with Maven.
